observations: A skull form fills most of the canvas, outlined in thick black lines, with the left eye socket holding layered white, grey, and red-orange shapes while the right socket shows a flat yellow-gold fill.
The skull's surface carries overlapping bands of teal, green, purple, and warm orange, with a row of white rectangular teeth at the lower jaw set against a cyan-edged gum line.
The lavender background is covered edge-to-edge in a dense tangle of looping black, blue, and yellow lines that sit behind the skull but press close to its outline on all sides.
reading: Two mismatched eye sockets—one busy with layered colour, one simply filled—give the skull an off-balance quality that reads as unease rather than symmetry. The warm bands crossing the face pull against the cool lavender field outside, and the surrounding line tangle feels less like decoration than like pressure closing in. The white teeth at the bottom hold their own quiet weight.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, the skull form links this work to title neighbor nnxyz nnotb #287, which also centres a skull on a patterned ground. The collector connects nnxyz's line-dense surfaces to scrimshaw through mark-over-mark patterning—that is the collector's reading, not a statement of the artist's intent.

connections.reason: Both centre a multi-colour skull with an open jaw showing white teeth, but #287 floats its form against soft bokeh circles while #286 presses it into a tight line-tangle background, making the containment feel different in each.
Both share a flat lavender ground and use rectangular white tooth shapes at the lower jaw, though the nifty-faces work builds its head from angular yellow blocks while #286 uses curved skull anatomy.

lookingQuestion: How does the difference between the two eye sockets—one layered with multiple colours and shapes, one filled with a single flat tone—affect the way you read the skull's face as a whole?
ambiguities: Small white linear marks inside the mouth opening may be a signature or incidental line work; image resolution does not resolve this clearly.
